All artwork, music, and sound effects in Geargrave Outlands were created with generative AI tools (images: OpenAI image models; music: Suno; sound effects: ElevenLabs) and then selected, edited, and integrated by the developer.
Pre-generated 3D models. The 3D models of the travel view (convoy and raider vehicles, roadside props, landmarks, ruins and war-zone set pieces, and the walking crew and roadside figures) were generated with Tripo3D (Tripo AI) from AI-generated reference images: model sheets made with the image models above, or the game's own AI-generated vehicle art. Tripo3D also rigged the figures and supplied their idle, walk and run animations. Every model was then reworked in Blender (rescaling and orienting, polygon reduction, re-baking the textures, fixing geometry) and ships as a fixed model file.
Story text was written with AI assistance and edited by the developer. All translations were produced with AI assistance. All of this content is pre-generated and ships as fixed files. The game does not generate any content with AI while you play.

The game's music was generated with an AI music tool (Suno). The text of this store page was written with the help of an AI assistant. No AI runs while you play, and the game does not connect to any AI service.

Generative AI tools were used during development to create part of what you see and hear: the portraits of the fictional players and their faces at different ages, background illustrations, the short ambient videos, the music, the commentator's recorded calls and the surnames he calls out —a synthetic voice that does not belong to any real person— and part of the art on this page. Everything was reviewed, trimmed and edited by hand before going in, and every commentator line was checked with speech recognition to make sure it says what it should. The sound effects are real public-domain recordings. The game does not generate anything with AI while you play.

Dealer's Choice was made by a solo developer working with AI assistance. AI tools helped write the game's code and in-game text, and the store artwork and achievement icons were rendered from 3D models built with AI assistance. All of this content was created during development and reviewed by the developer. Nothing in the game is generated by AI while you play.

Last Light uses pre-generated AI content. All voices are AI text-to-speech (ElevenLabs, OpenAI) performing the game's scripts; the music was generated with Suno; some sound effects with ElevenLabs; and several illustrations, portraits, the logo and store art with AI image tools. All of it was reviewed and edited by the developer. No content is generated while you play.

Generative AI was used to draft text only: the in-game interface strings, the achievement names and descriptions, their translations into 13 non-English languages, and this store page. All of it was reviewed and edited by the developer before release.
No AI-generated images, audio or video are used. This game ships with no image or audio files at all — every shape, sound and note is produced by the game's own code at run time.
Nothing is generated while you play. The game makes no network calls and contacts no AI service.

No AI image generators were used for the game's visuals. The clover, trees, and ground were modeled and textured in the 3D software Blender from the developer's own photos of the real thing, then assembled into a forest in Unity. The concept, the photography, and the decisions about how the game looks were all the developer's own.
Made with help from AI
• The game's code and the Blender scripts that build the shapes and textures. The developer checked the finished visuals side by side with the photos of the real thing.
• The text in the game and on the store page, and its translation from Japanese into 10 languages, including English. The translations were made by AI and checked by a different AI. No native speaker has reviewed them, so if you spot a mistranslation, please report it through the support contact.
The sounds are nature recordings made by other creators and released as CC0 or public domain. No AI runs while you play.

Our Approach to AI in Project Freefall
We incorporated AI into our creative workflow:
- A headstart for music, code, and  artistic concepts.
- Initial rendering for some characters and game assets
Why we used it:
- Brainstorming new and exciting concepts the community would like
- Speed to make sure we got assets within the game in the timeframe the community expected
Our talented team of artists, developers and designers brought the assets and concepts to the finish line.
This approach allows us to take more risks, move faster, and make more things the community wants.

At Lovely Bytes, we're not just developers, we're passionate gamers like you. And because we understand the gamer's perspective, we firmly believe that the heart of a truly great game lies in the emotional depth and authenticity that only human creativity can provide.
In the development of UNHEIM, artificial intelligence plays a supporting role to accelerate our production, and is used mindfully to help us with certain time-consuming tasks, such as visual brainstorming, or speeding up the process of creating some of the textures. Additionally, AI bravely tackles the Herculean task of turning our chaotic creative thoughts and wild brainstorming scribbles into something resembling coherent, actionable documents.
Our approach to AI is to use it as a tool to augment our skills and capabilities, not to substitute the craft elements that are crucial for creating a deeply engaging and memorable game experience.
Now go and have fun getting scared to death, knowing that what you experience is the result of a mindful blend of assistive technology and traditional craftsmanship.

AI was used to assist in translating the game's store page.
Some images are generated by artificial intelligence and refined by an illustrator.

This game uses generative AI tools to create certain visual assets, including paintings and fictional human portraits. These AI-generated images depict characters and artworks that do not represent real individuals. All assets were curated, edited, and integrated into the game by the development team.

During the development of this game AI generative tools were used to create and modify some of the in-game assets, based on the prompts and the source materials created by our artists.
Some of the text materials were also created and modified by the AI generative tools, primarily for proof reading and localization.
At Banana we use AI to help us develop our game in code, translations and background elements. No live AI systems are used in-game.
